title: Add safety-first tool calling examples (allowlist + validation) + production anti-patterns
author: Sabrina James
body: ## Summary This PR adds a safety-first set of tool calling examples across the canonical `redwood-examples` repo. The goal is to make the default copy/paste path secure: explicit allowlists, strict argument validation, redacted logging, and clear guidance on what NOT to do in production. This also closes the loop on support reports where customers copy older snippets that (a) dispatch tools by name without allowlisting, (b) try to parse tool args mid-stream, or (c) treat model-produced JSON as trusted input. ## Motivation We’re refreshing streaming/tool calling/structured output examples across SDKs. Tool calling examples are particularly sensitive because users tend to adapt them into production quickly. We want the canonical examples to enforce: (1) allowlist dispatch, (2) schema/validation for arguments, (3) safe logging and error messages, and (4) explicit “don’t do this” anti-patterns (shell exec, arbitrary network calls, tool-name reflection) without providing runnable insecure code. ## What’s included - New examples in Python/TypeScript/Go that demonstrate: - Tool definitions with tight, minimal parameter surfaces - Safe dispatch by allowlist (`map[name]handler` / `switch name`) - Strict arg validation (JSON Schema or language-native validation) prior to tool execution - Clear failures on unknown tools or invalid arguments - Redaction patterns for logs (avoid printing access tokens / customer content) - Notes on streaming: do not attempt to parse partial tool args deltas; only parse after tool call arguments are complete - New `SECURITY.md` (examples-focused) with guidance and non-goals. - README updates linking tool calling safety notes from the canonical tool calling pages. ## Not included - No examples that execute arbitrary shell commands, browse the public internet, or dynamically call functions by reflection based on model output. Those are called out as anti-patterns, but we intentionally do not provide runnable code for them. - No SDK API changes; this is examples + documentation only. ## Files / structure - `tools/python/safe_tool_dispatch.py`: allowlist + JSON schema validation helper used by the Python example. - `tools/typescript/safeToolDispatch.ts`: allowlist + Zod validation (kept dependency-light; Zod only for TS examples). - `tools/go/safetools/dispatch.go`: registry-based dispatcher + strict JSON decoding (disallow unknown fields). - `tool-calling/python/safe_weather_lookup.py`: safe tool calling walkthrough (single tool + unknown tool handling). - `tool-calling/typescript/safe_parallel_tools.ts`: parallel tool calls with concurrency limit + per-tool validation. - `tool-calling/go/safe_tool_router/main.go`: context-aware safe dispatch + timeout propagation. - `SECURITY.md`: “tool calling in production” guidance + anti-pattern list. ## Example snippet (TS dispatcher) ```ts const toolRegistry = { get_weather: { schema: WeatherArgs, handler: getWeather }, get_timezone: { schema: TimezoneArgs, handler: getTimezone }, } as const; export async function dispatchToolCall(name: string, rawArgs: unknown) { const entry = toolRegistry[name as keyof typeof toolRegistry]; if (!entry) { throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}. Refusing to execute.`); } const args = entry.schema.parse(rawArgs); return await entry.handler(args); } ``` ## Checklist - [x] Copy/paste runnable with minimal setup and explicit env vars - [x] No insecure patterns in runnable code - [x] Clearly document anti-patterns and why they’re unsafe - [x] Keep naming aligned with canonical docs (“tool calling”, not “function calling”) - [x] Add to snippet test runner manifest (mock server) ## Testing - `pnpm test:snippets` (TS) - `pytest -q` (Python) - `go test ./...` (Go) All run against the examples mock server in CI; no staging calls required. ## Notes for reviewers - Security review requested on the anti-pattern wording in `SECURITY.md` to ensure we warn without giving an easy copy/paste path to unsafe behaviors. - Also looking for feedback on the strictness of JSON parsing (Go: DisallowUnknownFields; TS: Zod strict objects; Py: jsonschema + additionalProperties false).
commits: examples(tool-calling): add SECURITY.md with tool calling do/don’t guidance
examples(py): safe tool dispatch helper with allowlist + jsonschema validation
examples(ts): safe parallel tool calling example with concurrency limit + zod validation
examples(go): safe tool registry dispatcher with strict json decoding
docs: link tool safety notes from tool-calling README and add redaction guidance
ci: register new snippets in snippet-test runner manifest
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): The allowlist pattern is good. Two nits: (1) In SECURITY.md, the “don’t run shell commands” section should also explicitly mention not to pass user input into interpreters (bash, powershell) even if you think you’re sanitizing. (2) Can we ensure our examples don’t log raw tool args on error? That can leak PII. Sabrina James (Author): Updated SECURITY.md to call out interpreters explicitly (bash/pwsh/python -c) and added a note that “sanitization is not sufficient.” Also updated all examples to log only tool name + validation error type; no raw args. Ibrahim Khan (DevEx): Please add an explicit note about streaming deltas: don’t `JSON.parse` tool args until complete. We keep seeing partial arg deltas in support tickets. Sabrina James (Author): Added a “Streaming note” section to each language example and a shared paragraph in README. Dana Lo (TS): Zod dependency is fine, but keep it pinned and documented. Also consider `.strict()` so unknown keys fail. Sabrina James (Author): Done: `z.object({...}).strict()` and pinned version in package.json for the TS examples workspace. Mateusz Zielinski (Go): Go decoder using `DisallowUnknownFields` is great. Please also cap body size / args size in the example to avoid unbounded memory usage when users adapt it. Sabrina James (Author): Added `io.LimitReader` in the Go example when decoding tool args and noted max size in comments. Marcus Lin (Security): Approving with the latest changes. Ibrahim Khan (DevEx): Approving. Dana Lo: Approving. Mateusz Zielinski: Approving.
release_notes: Canonical examples: added safety-first tool calling patterns with allowlists + argument validation and a new SECURITY.md outlining production anti-patterns.
